title: NeuroAtlas: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Clinical EEG and Brain-Computer Interfaces
abstract: arXiv:2605.14698v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Foundation models (FMs) promise to extract unified representations that generalize across downstream tasks. They have emerged across fields, including electroencephalography (EEG), but it is less clear how effective they are in this particular field. Published evaluations differ in datasets, in the EEG-specific preprocessing that might influence reported results, and in the reported metrics, frequently obscuring the clinical relevance in EEG. We introduce NeuroAtlas, the largest EEG benchmark to date: 42 datasets and 260k hours covering clinical EEG (epilepsy, sleep medicine, brain age estimation) and brain-computer interfaces, and include multiple datasets per task along with bespoke clinical evaluation metrics. Besides evaluating EEG-FMs with respect to supervised baselines, we present results from generic time-series FMs. We report three findings. translated_title: NeuroAtlas：面向临床脑电图与脑机接口的基础模型基准测试
translated_abstract: 基础模型有望提取可跨下游任务泛化的统一表示。它们已在包括脑电图（EEG）在内的多个领域涌现，但它们在这一特定领域的效果尚不明确。已发表的评估在数据集、可能影响结果的脑电图专用预处理方法以及所报告的指标上各不相同，这常常掩盖了脑电图研究中的临床相关性。我们推出了NeuroAtlas，这是迄今为止规模最大的脑电图基准：涵盖42个数据集和26万小时的数据，包括临床脑电图（癫痫、睡眠医学、脑年龄估计）和脑机接口，并为每个任务提供多个数据集以及专门定制的临床评估指标。除了将脑电图基础模型与有监督基线进行对比评估外，我们还展示了通用时间序列基础模型的结果。我们报告了三个发现。首先，脑电图专用基础模型并不总是稳定地优于时间序列基础模型……
tldr: 本文提出迄今最大的脑电图基准NeuroAtlas（涵盖42个数据集、26万小时数据），系统评估后发现脑电图专用基础模型并不稳定地优于通用时间序列基础模型。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces NeuroAtlas, the largest EEG benchmark to date covering 42 datasets and 260k hours, and finds that EEG-specific foundation models do not consistently outperform generic time-series foundation models.
